stories.headline: Exploring the potential of immunotherapy in early-stage triple-negative breast cancer
stories.what_happened: Triple-negative breast cancers, which are more frequently diagnosed in younger women, are a subtype of breast tumor characterized by the absence of hormone receptors and HER2 overexpression. As a result, they do not respond to hormone therapy or HER2-targeted treatments. Their prognosis is generally less favorable than that of other breast cancer subtypes.

stories.headline: Hemoglobin component heme shown to inhibit enzyme that helps dissolve blood clots
stories.what_happened: When it comes to blood clots, it is not only how they form that is crucial, but also how the body can break them down again. A team of researchers at the University of Koblenz, led by Prof. Dr. Marie-T. Hopp, has demonstrated that heme—a component of hemoglobin—can influence this process. The findings, published in the International Journal of Biological Macromolecules, provide a new molecular approach to better understanding the link between hemolysis and an increased risk of thrombosis.
